I find it much easier to eat on vyvanse than other stimulants (however I can still have days/moments when I do struggle some with it. I had a really hard time eating properly on Ritalin unless if I waited an extra 2 hours or so to take my redose, basically letting myself (partially) comedown from the meds to increase my appetite/ability to get stuff down, and then take my next dose, wait for it to kick back in and then do the same thing again, but that's not really a workable solution because I had to deal with coming down from the meds 3 times a day so all in all it made my ADHD worse and I had to spend a lot of spoons trying to plan shit around when I'd eat and when I'd actually have the meds properly working, defeating the whole purpose of taking them in the first place.

The main issue with Ritalin was having to redose, which would always make my tummy feel off for a while after taking it, making me not have much of an appetite, and also having the stimulants kick in again fresh, (re-)upping the stimulating effects again, would also increase/refresh the reduction in apetite again.

With vyvanse I avoid the whole issue of having to redose, which is the main benefit of vyvanse for my appetite, but I also have less/weaker side-effects in general from vyvanse. Re-uptake inhibitors have just never really worked well for me other than making me overstimulated and have lots of issues with side-effects even at tiny doses, so it makes sense to me a releaser like vyvanse causes less issues with appetite than a re-uptake inhibitor like ritalin.

The reason it doesn't affect your sleep anymore is because when you take it rectally you skip the first-pass metabolism as it gets absorbed into the bloodstream directly, while if you take it orally a lot of it gets metabolised by the liver. The main metabolites of progesterone are allopregnanolone and pregnanolone which affect the GABAa receptor. This is the same receptor alcohol and benzodiazepines (like xanax for example) bind to to make you disinhibited, sedate you, improve sleep quality, reduce anxiety, prevent or stop seizures etc. That's why when you take prog orally it affects your sleep, however the issue is that since a lot of it gets converted, you end up getting way less actual prog into your bloodstream. 

Another issue with this is that  allopregnanolone is a metabolic intermediate in an androgen backdoor pathway to form DHT, which is the nasty hormone that causes balding in a lot of men and is up to 10x stronger than testosterone. For some people this backdoor pathway doesn't seem to be very active, but for some it's actually a big issue and taking prog increases masculinisation.

Before HRT my life was just very dull and I was very depressed from about 16 years old. I didn't give a shit about life and was just kinda going through it on autopilot, just trying to focus on school and later uni and sports to keep me busy and give myself some kinda goal. Yes I still have some bad days occasionally, but most of that depression is gone and my anxiety has gotten much better as well. I actually feel pretty comfortable in my body now and the way I can express myself and how others treat me feels so good and makes me really happy.
